video_title: Doug Christie addresses Kings' margin for error, turnovers | NBC Sports California

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on Kings' first-quarter struggles against defensive pressure
quotes.excerpt: they started blitzing Darius and trying to take him out of the game
quotes.quote: Getting off in the first quarter, I think we tried to play some toss, some splits because they started blitzing Darius and trying to take him out of the game. Unfortunately, E-Man got into a little bit of foul trouble there early on. After that first quarter, which was a blitz, the second and third quarter was more along the lines, but we got to bottle up that and figure out a way to get that for 48 minutes. That's the key.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie says the Kings need to figure out how to play with consistent intensity for all 48 minutes after struggling against defensive pressure in the first quarter.

structured.context: Doug Christie discusses the Kings' struggles against defensive blitzes directed at Darius Garland.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the need for better offensive spacing against blitzes
quotes.excerpt: you need three outlets when they're going to blitz Darius
quotes.quote: You need three outlets when they're going to blitz Darius. It's the roller who's setting the screen, somebody has to come up out of the corner. I think we were a little late on everything in that first half, even on the rotations. We have to be aggressive, and that was something that we went over in practice. It's something that we looked at in film and talked to them about, but you got to give them credit. They've won championships, they know exactly what they want to do.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie explains that the Kings need better spacing and three outlets when opponents blitz Darius Garland to maintain their offensive advantage.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains the need for better offensive spacing and rotations when opponents blitz Darius Garland.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the impact of high turnover rates
quotes.excerpt: 20 turnovers for 26 points is never going to do it
quotes.quote: We have to take care of the basketball at a really, really high level because our margin for error is not huge, but 20 turnovers for 26 points is never going to do it. We got to take care of that basketball.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the Kings turnover issues: 20 turnovers for 26 points is never going to do it. He says the team must take care of the basketball at a high level.

structured.context: Doug Christie emphasizes the need for the team to reduce turnovers to maintain a competitive margin for error.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on defensive adjustments for Darius
quotes.excerpt: Darius is going to continue to see every defense that that you can create
quotes.quote: I think you're going to see it more. I think Darius is going to continue to see every defense that that you can create. They were blitzing small-small, they were blitzing small-big, so it didn't matter. If it was a five-man they were blitzing, if it was a small they were blitzing. I think probably haven't seen the small-small blitz, but even that goes for not only Darius, but it goes for the screener. Where are you going once that happens? You got to release and find an area that he can pass you the basketball, coming up out of the corner. We got to make sure that we make ourselves available because once he gets off the basketball, you put two on the ball, now you have the advantage. But if you don't recognize it quickly enough or you don't make the pass, then you lose the advantage.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie expects teams to keep blitzing Darius Garland and says the team must recognize the defensive pressure faster to capitalize on the resulting advantage.

structured.context: Doug Christie analyzes the defensive blitzing strategies used against Darius Garland and the necessary offensive responses.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on E-Man's physical style and rookie development
quotes.excerpt: E-Man, he plays a physical style of basketball and I tell him to don't back up
quotes.quote: E-Man, he plays a physical style of basketball and I tell him to don't back up. Trying to work with him, talk with him about what he's going to see on a night-to-night basis and what the referees are going to be calling. Unfortunately, he got his second and then later in the second half, I believe he got his fourth. So it was just kind of seeing how far we were going to go with him, but love what he brings, love all of the intangibles that he brings to the game. It's being a rookie, you got to learn the the flow of the game and how to survive out there without getting yourself in foul trouble.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie discusses rookie E-Man's physical style of play and the challenge of learning how to stay on the floor without getting into foul trouble.

structured.context: Doug Christie discusses the physical play and foul trouble experienced by rookie E-Man.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on maintaining urgency and pace
quotes.excerpt: making sure to Shon's point, making ourselves available when they begin to blitz us
quotes.quote: More than anything, just talking about the things that that we can control. Not turning the basketball over, making sure to Shon's point, making ourselves available when they begin to blitz us, playing with a more sense of urgency as far as pace, getting into our stuff quicker so that we're not deeper into the shot clock and all of a sudden you're finding yourself in butter clock, which is seven or under and you're rushing shots. The quicker we can get into it, and then obviously getting defensive stops and getting out and running because now they're cross-matching and different things. You're rim running with your bigs, and if you can seal a small down there, you got the advantage. The same things that that they do.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie emphasizes the need for the Kings to play with more urgency and get into their offensive sets quicker to avoid rushing shots late in the clock.

structured.context: Doug Christie outlines the team's need for better pace, urgency, and ball security to avoid late shot clock situations.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on Draymond Green's offensive execution
quotes.excerpt: Draymond has run that offense for the number of years at a really, really high level
quotes.quote: Draymond has run that offense for the number of years at a really, really high level. So if you make a mistake, he's going to make you pay for it.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the challenge of facing Draymond Green: If you make a mistake he is going to make you pay for it.

structured.context: Doug Christie praises Draymond Green for his high-level execution of the offense.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on De'Anthony Melton's long pass and defensive breakdown
quotes.excerpt: I think he leaked out, I don't think it was anything that guys didn't do
quotes.quote: I think he leaked out. I don't think it was anything that guys didn't do. He just leaked out. Everyone's looking at the basketball, trying to rebound, offensive rebound because we wanted to crash and make sure that we were emphasizing that. That's an area we wanted to get at least 15, we got 12 of them tonight, but he got behind the defense and they just threw it long.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie breaks down a defensive breakdown where De'Anthony Melton got behind the defense on a long pass while the Kings were crashing the glass.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains a defensive breakdown that allowed De'Anthony Melton to get behind the defense.
